title: Chloramphenicol

indications.title: Conjunctivitis
notes: Linked prescribing pathway: conjunctivitis — Adults & children >1 month 1st line

regimens.duration: Continue use until 48 hours after infection has cleared (typically 5-10 days)

cautions: Avoid repeated courses and prolonged treatment

interactions.description: Chloramphenicol potentially increases the anticoagulant effect of Acenocoumarol. Manufacturer makes no recommendation.

intravenous Chloramphenicol increases the concentration of Fosphenytoin and Fosphenytoin affects the concentration of intravenous Chloramphenicol. Manufacturer advises monitor concentration and adjust dose.
Chloramphenicol is predicted to increase the exposure to Glibenclamide. Manufacturer advises monitor blood glucose.
Chloramphenicol is predicted to increase the exposure to Gliclazide. Manufacturer advises monitor blood glucose.
Chloramphenicol is predicted to increase the exposure to Glimepiride. Manufacturer advises monitor blood glucose.
Chloramphenicol is predicted to increase the exposure to Glipizide. Manufacturer advises monitor blood glucose.
Chloramphenicol is predicted to increase the exposure to Guanfacine. Manufacturer advises adjust Guanfacine dose.
Chloramphenicol decreases the efficacy of Iron. Manufacturer makes no recommendation.
Phenobarbital decreases the concentration of Chloramphenicol. Manufacturer makes no recommendation.

intravenous Chloramphenicol increases the concentration of Phenytoin and Phenytoin affects the concentration of intravenous Chloramphenicol. Manufacturer advises monitor concentration and adjust dose.
Primidone decreases the concentration of Chloramphenicol. Manufacturer makes no recommendation.
Rifampicin decreases the concentration of Chloramphenicol. Manufacturer advises caution.
Chloramphenicol increases the concentration of Tacrolimus. Manufacturer makes no recommendation.
Chloramphenicol is predicted to increase the exposure to Tolbutamide. Manufacturer advises monitor blood glucose.
Chloramphenicol potentially increases the anticoagulant effect of Warfarin. Manufacturer makes no recommendation.

effects: Aplastic anaemia (reversible or irreversible, with reports of resulting leukaemia)
Angioedema; bone marrow disorders; eye stinging; fever; paraesthesia; skin reactions
Bone marrow disorders; circulatory collapse; diarrhoea; enterocolitis; nausea; optic neuritis; oral disorders; ototoxicity; vomiting
Agranulocytosis; bone marrow disorders; depression; diarrhoea; dry mouth; fungal superinfection; headache; nausea; nerve disorders; thrombocytopenic purpura; urticaria; vision disorders; vomiting

renalConsiderations: Caution (increased risk of bone-marrow depression)—monitor plasma-chloramphenicol concentration. M
hepaticConsiderations: Manufacturer advises caution (increased risk of bone-marrow depression)—monitor plasma-chloramphenicol concentration.
pregnancyBreastfeeding: Manufacturer advises avoid; neonatal ‘grey-baby syndrome’ if used in third trimester.
Avoid unless essential—no information on topical use but risk of ‘neonatal grey-baby syndrome’ with oral use in third trimester.
Manufacturer advises avoid; use another antibiotic; may cause bone-marrow toxicity in infant; concentration in milk usually insufficient to cause ‘grey syndrome’.
Avoid unless essential— theoretical risk of bone-marrow toxicity.
practicalPoints: Plasma concentration monitoring preferred in the elderly.
Plasma concentration monitoring preferred in those under 4 years of age.

Recommended peak plasma concentration (approx. 2 hours after administration by mouth, intravenous injection or infusion) 10–25 mg/litre; pre-dose (‘trough’) concentration should not exceed 15 mg/litre.
Blood counts required before and periodically during treatment.
Displacement value may be significant for injection, consult local guidelines. For intermittent intravenous infusion , dilute reconstituted solution further in Glucose 5% or Sodium Chloride 0.9%. M
